The '''linear range''' of a function is the portion of its overall range where the input is [[directly proportional]] to the output.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Handbook of plastics analysis |date=2003 |publisher=Dekker |isbn=978-0-8247-0708-8 |editor-last=Lobo |editor-first=Hubert |location=New York Basel}}</ref> The concept of a linear range is important in analytical science where it can apply to measuring equipment or chemical reactions.{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}}

[[File:LinearRange.png|alt=A graph with a black curved line labeled Real. The x-axis is labeled Input and the y-axis is labeled Output. On top of the black curved line is a blue straight line labeled Linear that matches part of the black curved line. The section where they match is labeled linear range.|thumb|A graph showing the linear range of an input]]
